question: What is the difference between an atom and a molecule?
learning_objectives: Define an atom and a molecule.
Explain how atoms combine to form molecules.
Distinguish between elements, compounds, atoms, and molecules using examples.
concepts: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that still has that element’s chemical identity.
A molecule is a group of two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
Molecules can contain atoms of the same element, such as oxygen gas, or atoms of different elements, such as water.
Not all substances are made of separate molecules; for example, salts like sodium chloride form large repeating ionic structures rather than individual molecules.
reasoning_steps: Start with an atom: it is a single particle of an element, such as one hydrogen atom or one oxygen atom.
When atoms form chemical bonds with each other, they can make a molecule.
If two oxygen atoms bond together, they form an oxygen molecule, O2.
If two hydrogen atoms bond with one oxygen atom, they form a water molecule, H2O.
So, an atom is one basic unit, while a molecule is made from two or more bonded atoms.
assumptions: The explanation is using basic high-school chemistry definitions.
The term molecule refers to atoms held together by chemical bonds as a distinct unit.
common_misconceptions: Misconception: All molecules are compounds. Correction: A molecule like O2 has only one element, so it is not a compound.
Misconception: All substances are made of molecules. Correction: Some substances, like metals and ionic salts, are made of extended structures rather than separate molecules.
Misconception: An atom is always found alone. Correction: Many atoms are usually found bonded to other atoms in molecules or larger structures.
key_takeaways: An atom is a single unit of an element.
A molecule is two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
Molecules may be made of the same kind of atom or different kinds of atoms.
